subsystems.name: World model
subsystems.role: an explicit, updatable model of the organisation, its market and its competitors, used to predict what a decision would do.

subsystems.name: Perception and data layer
subsystems.role: turns messy organisational signals into structured state the agent can reason over.

subsystems.name: Reasoning core
subsystems.role: decomposes a strategic question into sub-problems and proposes candidate actions.

subsystems.name: Memory
subsystems.role: stores past decisions and their outcomes so the agent does not repeat mistakes.
parts: knowledge graph of entities and relations
case history of decisions and results

subsystems.name: Verification and self-correction loop
subsystems.role: replaces the executive's judgement with simulated consequence-checking and adversarial critique.

subsystems.name: Action and tool layer
subsystems.role: lets proposals actually change systems, under permissions.

subsystems.name: Governance and audit
subsystems.role: keeps decisions traceable, reviewable and accountable to humans and regulators.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the organisation
buildSteps.detail: Connect financial, operational and market systems into one consistent schema, so the agent sees the same numbers the executives do.

buildSteps.title: Build a simulatable model of the business
buildSteps.detail: Fit a causal or simulation model that can be calibrated against past decisions and asked 'what would have happened if...'.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the reasoning core
buildSteps.detail: Take a large foundation model, give it tools (search, calculation, database queries) and fine-tune it on the organisation's own decision records where they exist.

buildSteps.title: Add memory and retrieval
buildSteps.detail: Index past memos, board papers and outcomes so proposals are grounded in the organisation's real history rather than generic advice.

buildSteps.title: Wire in self-correction
buildSteps.detail: Have the agent generate several candidate plans, run each through the simulator and a critic model, and revise until constraints and forecasts hold.

buildSteps.title: Run in shadow mode
buildSteps.detail: For months, let the agent produce recommendations that are never acted on, and compare them against what the humans actually chose and what happened.

buildSteps.title: Grant bounded authority
buildSteps.detail: Give the agent write access only to reversible, well-modelled decisions — pricing rules, staffing rosters, inventory — with human approval above a threshold.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and govern
buildSteps.detail: Track accuracy, drift in the model's assumptions and every action taken, with an escalation path when confidence is low.

prerequisites.why: current agents handle tasks of minutes to hours; strategy spans quarters and feedback arrives too late for naive reinforcement learning.
few firms have a coherent, live model of their own operations to simulate decisions against.
correlation is not enough; the agent must estimate what a decision causes, not just what it correlates with.
unlike a game with a score, strategic quality may only be knowable years later, making it hard to train or verify.
someone must answer legally and ethically for a decision, and that attribution is unresolved for autonomous agents.
training and serving large agentic models at enterprise scale is expensive but technically feasible today.

pathway.milestone: copilots that summarise, forecast and draft analysis while a human decides
pathway.unlocks: time savings and better-prepared human judgement, with no delegation of authority.

pathway.milestone: agents executing bounded, reversible workflows with approval gates
pathway.unlocks: measurable reliability data on which decisions can safely be delegated.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop optimisation in narrow operational domains such as pricing, scheduling and supply chain
pathway.unlocks: fast feedback loops where outcomes are measurable within days.

pathway.milestone: agents advising on genuine strategy, with simulation-checked reasoning and full audit trails
pathway.unlocks: faster strategy cycles — still with human executives accountable for the call.
possible only if verification, liability and evaluation problems are solved; otherwise it remains assistance, not replacement.
